FIRST partners with Qualcomm, Disney and REV Robotics on next-generation K–8 programs

Arduino technology and a new build platform will support the 2027–2028 season, with transitional compatibility for existing SPIKE sets.

FIRST ↗18 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

A new partnership for young learners

On November 18, FIRST announced expanded collaboration with Qualcomm Technologies for next-generation K–8 robotics experiences. The announcement identifies a spring 2027 launch and preparation for the 2027–2028 season. Plans distinguish ages 5–7 and 8–14, emphasizing collaborative building, testing and iteration.

Technology and game-design roles

Qualcomm is the lead technology partner through Arduino, REV Robotics is developing the physical build system, and Walt Disney Imagineering will contribute games, challenges and annual themes. The program FAQ identifies an Arduino UNO Q-based hardware platform for grades 3–8. FIRST remains responsible for the learning experience and delivery community.

A transition for existing equipment

FIRST plans compatibility with LEGO Education SPIKE Prime and Essential through the 2028–2029 season, while clarifying that the new programs are not affiliated with or endorsed by LEGO. Program names, pricing and participation details remain forthcoming. Schools can use the announcement for transition planning, rather than assuming the new kits are already available.
